description: The command PowerUp registers in ~/.claude/settings.json for its hook script: the script path in single quotes, each single quote in it written as '\'' (one that a combining scalar follows is not a match, as Foundation's replacingOccurrences finds it). Claude Code runs the command through a shell, and the path holds a space ("Application Support").
function: HookInstaller.hookCommand() — input the hook script's path, expected the command string
verifiedBy: DESIGN.md v1.6, v2.14; Tests/PowerUpTests/HookFixtureTests.swift testHookCommandTable points the support directory at the path's folder and reads HookInstaller.hookCommand(). Rust: rust/powerup-core/tests/hooks.rs hook_command_cases runs hooks::hook_command.
capturedAgainst: Swift 5.9.2 Foundation (Xcode 15.2) on macOS 27.2, PowerUp at 2dd77aa

cases.name: a path with a space is single-quoted
cases.reason: The support folder is under "Application Support": unquoted, the shell splits the path and every hook dies with exit 127 (HK-181).

cases.name: a single quote in the path is closed, escaped and reopened
cases.reason: Inside single quotes nothing escapes, so an embedded quote is written as '\'' (HK-181).

cases.name: every single quote is escaped
cases.reason: Each quote gets its own close, escaped quote and reopen.

cases.name: a path without spaces is quoted too
cases.reason: The command is always quoted, so the registered string never depends on the path's characters.

cases.name: a quote that a combining mark follows is not escaped
cases.reason: Foundation's replacingOccurrences never matches a quote that a combining scalar extends into another character (measured on macOS 27.2); the core keeps that rule.

cases.name: a quote that a spacing mark follows is escaped
cases.reason: Only a Grapheme_Cluster_Break=Extend scalar after a quote stops Foundation's match; a spacing mark joins the quote's Character but does not (measured against every scalar, found by the #158 differential).

cases.name: a quote that a ZWJ follows is escaped
cases.reason: A ZWJ after the quote does not stop Foundation's match either.

cases.name: a quote after a prepended scalar is escaped
cases.reason: A Prepend scalar before the quote makes one Character of the two, yet Foundation still replaces the quote.

cases.name: non-ASCII path characters are kept as they are
cases.reason: The command is the path's own text; only quotes change. The accent is decomposed because the platform's file URL spells it so (the script path the app passes is URL.path).
